note: A number known only at runtime now takes the unit the same number written as a literal takes, instead of reaching its CSS variable bare: <Box p={m} /> with m = 2 pads by 8px, as p={2} does, where it used to set padding: 2, which is no CSS length. Spacing and sizes are multiplied by 4 into px, durations take ms, and unitless properties, colors and custom properties keep the number; a string holding only a number ('2') converts like a literal string does, other strings and null, undefined or false pass through unchanged. This holds in responsive arrays, selectors, conditionals and Devup UI's own styled() callbacks and templates. Intentional behavior change: a number a Devup UI styled() callback returns at runtime used to read as px (3 → 3px) and is now on the spacing scale a written number is on (3 → 12px). The conversion is imported, once per file that needs it, from the new dependency-free @devup-ui/react/scale subpath (<package>/scale under a custom package option), which also serves React Native's conversion; no function is declared in the output. Values the build knows still compile to static classes, and Emotion, styled-components and vanilla-extract files keep their px numbers.
